text.p: These are the leading stories in Zambia's press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Central Bank urges the government to maintain tight controls in the conduct of monetary and fiscal policies if economic development is to be realised.
- Workers at Copperbelt University in the northern mining town of Kitwe call off a two-day strike.
- Anglo American Corp (central Africa) Ltd managing director Anderson Mazoka says Zambia is unlikely to bring inflation down to 30 percent this year unless the local currency firms.
- The Food and Agricultural Organisation challenges the goverment to start thinking of where it will access grain to meet an anticipated food shortfall this year.
